newsitem.title: USA: Troubled Fla. cities should pay oversight - official.
newsitem.headline: Troubled Fla. cities should pay oversight - official.

text.p: Lt. Gov. Buddy MacKay has proposed that troubled cities reimburse the state for money spent by state-appointed financial oversight boards.
MacKay, who heads the oversight board guiding Miami's fiscal recovery, said oversight board expenses should be treated as a loan to cities in distress.

His proposal, which has not yet been submitted to the legislature in bill form, would amend the law that allows the governor to appoint an oversight board for cities that have budget deficits in two consecutive years.

Gov. Lawton Chiles used the law for the first time in December after Miami revealed a $68 million deficit in its $275 million budget. The current law does not spell out who should pay for oversight board expenses.
MacKay told The Miami Herald that other Florida taxpayers would probably object to subsidizing "the taxpayers of someplace that was incompetent."
The Miami oversight board has already spent $23,000 in travel costs and signed contracts to spend at least $451,000 for lawyers and financial advisers.
